The following scenario describes the temperature \(u\) of a rod at position \(x\) and time \(t\). Consider the equation \(u_t=u_{xx}\), \(0 < x < 1\), \(t > 0\), with boundary conditions \(u(0,t)=0, u(1,t)=0\). Suppose \(u(x,0)=\sin(n \pi x)\)
That is, an input data of frequency \(n\). Suppose \(V(t)\) denotes the maximum variation of temperature on the rod at time \(t\), that is, the maximum temperature minus the lowest temperature. We are interested as to what happens as \(n\) grows. What is your intuition as to the behavior of \(V(t)\):
options: As \(t \to \infty\), \(V(t)\) goes to zero slower for larger \(n\).
As \(t \to \infty\), \(V(t)\) goes to zero faster for larger \(n\).

questions.q: Suppose we have \(u_t=a^2 u_{xx}\), \(0 < x < 1, t > 0\), boundary conditions are \(u(0,t)=u(1,t)=0\), and the initial condition is \(u(x,0)=\sin(\pi x)\). What will be the behavior of \(u(x,t)\) as time increases. There may be more than one correct answer. You do not need to solve the equation to answer this question.
options: The solution decreases to minus infinity.
The solution does not change as time goes on.
For a fixed t, the solution will look kind of like an inverted parabola.
For a fixed t, the solution will be linear
For a fixed t, the second x derivative, \(u_{xx}\), will take on both signs.
For a fixed t, the second x derivative, \(u_{xx}\), will always be negative.  K. None of the above
